name: Montenegro

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 623327 inhabitants, recorded as 0.623 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Montenegrin, in the transversal venues pass, and it closes the case the pass of 2026-07-27 had to leave open. One unit, a stage. The value does not move — the previous pass had guessed 1 and refused to record it — but it stops being a guess, which is the whole of the change. What blocked the first attempt was a dead domain, not a dead server. Every route tried then went through gradskopozoriste.me, which answers a launching-soon page, and through the festival site, and both were read as 503. The theatre's live site is pgpozoriste.me, and it is unreachable from here on any tool — the connection is reset before TLS. So the reading was made entirely off the founder, which is better anyway: the Glavni grad Podgorica lists JU Gradsko pozorište among its javne ustanove, at Bokeška 2, with its director named, and the city's own repertoire notice for April 2026 sets out the scenes one by one — the Dramska scena za djecu, the Index scena, and the Lutkarska scena za djecu, which played Ružno pače on 18 April, Čarobni kamen on 24 and 25, and Pomelo, mali ružičasti slon on 26. A named puppet scene, currently producing, inside a municipal public institution: that is the denominator met. The lineage was read in Radoslav Lazić's survey of puppetry in Montenegro, and it is worth having because it dates the scene rather than the theatre. Šćućkin founded the first children's theatre at Cetinje in 1939; the Pionirsko pozorište followed in Podgorica on 12 January 1951; it merged into the Pionirski kulturni centar in 1959; in 1994 it separated again as the Dječije pozorište and took a Večernja scena beside the Dramska scena za djecu and the Lutkarska scena za djecu; in 2002 it became the Gradsko pozorište with those three scenes. The puppet scene is therefore at least thirty-two years old under that name and was not invented by the 2002 reorganisation. One thing does not fit the denominator cleanly and is recorded rather than smoothed over: the venue. Gradsko pozorište has no house of its own — one is under construction, sixty-five years after the founding — and the puppet scene plays in the Dodest hall of the KIC Budo Tomović, a different municipal institution. The point on the map is the theatre's seat at Bokeška 2, not where the puppets play. Under the old wording, which asked for a building of its own, this unit would have failed on the parent rather than on itself; under the ruling of 2026-07-27 a named permanent stage counts, and it does. Nothing else in the country reaches the denominator, and Lazić's survey is what makes that a finding rather than an absence of searching, because it is looking for exactly this. The Nikšićko lutkarsko pozorište Šćućkin was launched in 2013 on the initiative of the Ćano Koprivica foundation and played its first production in a music school; Pozorištance Škatula in Igalo is one animator, Željko Vavić, twenty years and five thousand performances, and no institution; the Herceg Novi work of 2013 came out of the Podi art puppet colony as a one-off; the Kotor children's theatre festival, running since 1993, is a festival, and festivals are excluded by name; the puppetry studies at the Cetinje drama faculty were introduced in 2009-10 and discontinued for want of staff. Four of those five are real puppetry and none of them is a permanent unit with public backing.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. The Faculty of Dramatic Arts in Cetinje, a unit of the state University of Montenegro and autonomous since 1997, offers acting, theatre and screen directing, production and dramaturgy at undergraduate and specialist level. No puppetry programme. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1, the detailed curriculum not having been read. Estimate.

For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90. notes: The puppet scene of the Podgorica city theatre, one of its three scenes since 2002 and named as such since 1994. It plays in the KIC Budo Tomović; the theatre's own house is still being built.

venues: re-read pgpozoriste.me when it answers. The question is narrow — does JU Gradsko pozorište name a permanent lutkarska scena, and does it hold puppeteers? The public status and the address are already established from podgorica.me. If the puppet stage is confirmed the value becomes 1, unit stage, parent JU Gradsko pozorište, at Bokeška 2.
